sentenceSets.sentence: A dilettante in the truest sense, he pursued every subject with enthusiasm and none to mastery.

answerChoices.reasoning: Enthusiast describes someone passionate about something; while he is enthusiastic, dilettante more specifically means superficial interest without deep mastery.
Amateur describes someone not professional; while he is amateur, dilettante more specifically implies superficial dabbling across multiple subjects.
Novice describes someone new to an activity; while he is novice-like, dilettante more specifically implies repeated superficial engagement with multiple subjects.
Dabbler is very close and describes engaging in multiple activities superficially; however, dilettante more specifically implies a cultured person with superficial interest in fine arts.
Learner describes someone acquiring knowledge; while he learns, dilettante more specifically means superficial engagement rather than sincere learning effort.
Generalist describes someone with broad rather than deep knowledge; while he is generalist-like, dilettante more specifically implies superficial interest rather than knowledgeable breadth.
Explorer describes investigating multiple things; while he explores, dilettante more specifically implies superficial engagement without depth.
Spectator describes someone watching rather than participating; while he may seem to spectate, dilettante implies active but superficial engagement.
Expert describes someone with deep knowledge and skill; the sentence contrasts with his lack of mastery.
Specialist describes someone focused deeply on one subject; the sentence shows engagement with multiple subjects without mastery.
Master describes achieving high skill; the sentence explicitly states he achieved mastery in none of his pursuits.

Enthusiast describes passionate engagement; while he engages, dilettante more specifically means superficial engagement motivated by social status.

Amateur describes non-professional engagement; while his engagement is amateur, dilettante more specifically implies superficial dabbling across multiple interests.

Socialite describes someone prominent in social circles; while he engages socially, dilettante more specifically describes superficial artistic engagement.

Dedicated means committed seriously; the sentence shows engagement without serious intention.
Serious describes earnest engagement; the sentence explicitly states he never engaged with serious intention.
